content.text:
The NASA Exoplanet Archive holds **21 separate published parameter sets** for HD 189733 b.

Of the three parameters checked, the **orbital period** shows the largest disagreement, in terms of statistical tension: the most discrepant pair (Kokori et al. 2023 vs. Stassun et al. 2017) differs by **4.75σ**, the biggest tension score of the set — even though the raw spread in period values is small in percentage terms (0.9% of the median), the tiny quoted uncertainties on individual period measurements make that gap statistically large.

If you instead judge disagreement by **fractional spread** (range as a percent of the typical value), **planet radius** is the largest outlier: values run from 12.3 to 14.12 R⊕, a 14.3% spread, with a 4.06σ tension between Stassun et al. 2017 and Bouchy et al. 2005.

Planet mass is the best-behaved parameter: its most discrepant pair (Bonomo et al. 2017 vs. Rosenthal et al. 2021) agrees within 0.7σ, so the archive's own uncertainty bars explain the spread there.
